contentSources.name: Local filesystem library
contentSources.performanceRights: Venue must hold PRO licences (ASCAP / BMI / SESAC / GMR) for public performance; owning the file is not a performance right.
contentSources.notes: Ingest via beets + Chromaprint/AcoustID + MusicBrainz for reliable tags and de-duplication. Widest format spread, so FFmpeg/libsndfile decoding is unavoidable.

contentSources.name: OpenSubsonic / Subsonic servers
contentSources.performanceRights: Same as local media - the server is transport, not a licence.
contentSources.notes: Navidrome (GPL-3.0, 23k stars), gonic (GPL-3.0) and others already implement it, including server-side jukebox mode. The jukeboxMediaTypes extension widens jukeboxControl beyond song IDs to podcast episodes and radio stations. We should both consume and expose this API.

contentSources.name: Jamendo
contentSources.access: Public REST API, free client ID
contentSources.performanceRights: CC terms per track; commercial/venue use may require Jamendo's licensing product. Attribution and share-alike obligations vary by track.
contentSources.notes: 500,000+ CC tracks with streaming-ready URLs. The best candidate for shipping a demo install that is legal out of the box.

contentSources.name: Free Music Archive
contentSources.performanceRights: Per-track CC licence, exposed in the API response.
contentSources.notes: Metadata includes licence type, which maps directly onto our per-track licence-class tagging requirement (H2).

contentSources.name: ccMixter
contentSources.notes: Remix- and stem-friendly catalog, which pairs unusually well with a stem-capable engine.

contentSources.name: Beatport / Beatsource
contentSources.performanceRights: Subscription grants DJ performance use within approved applications. Beatsource is being folded into Beatport.
contentSources.notes: Integrated into Serato, rekordbox, Traktor, VirtualDJ, djay, Engine OS and CDJ-3000 class hardware. Requires a commercial agreement; we ship the provider interface, not an implementation.

contentSources.name: TIDAL
contentSources.notes: The most widely integrated hi-fi option across DJ software.

contentSources.name: SoundCloud Go+
contentSources.performanceRights: Go+ content requires a separate written agreement with SoundCloud; the API terms mandate attribution and permalink backlinks and forbid circumventing quotas.
contentSources.notes: Explicitly documented as needing a written agreement - a good example of why streaming adapters must be optional plugins.

contentSources.name: DJ record pools (BPM Supreme, ZIPDJ)
contentSources.performanceRights: Subscription grants professional DJs the right to play downloaded music live, on radio and in streamed mixes.
contentSources.notes: Roughly $20-25/month. Downloads land in the local library, so no special runtime integration is needed - only licence-class tagging.

contentSources.name: Consumer streaming (Spotify, Apple Music personal accounts)
contentSources.performanceRights: NONE for public performance. Personal, non-commercial use only.
contentSources.notes: This is the fatal flaw in the Festify / Jukestar / PartyPlay class of open-source jukeboxes. CrowdDeck must refuse this path for venue mode by design.

contentSources.name: Media downloaders (yt-dlp and similar)
contentSources.performanceRights: None. Terms-of-service violation plus unlicensed public performance.
contentSources.notes: Explicitly out of scope for the venue product.

contentSources.name: Live MIDI instruments
contentSources.performanceRights: Live-performance licensing is separate from jukebox licensing; original material needs none.
contentSources.notes: The brief's distinguishing idea: a keyboard, groovebox or drum machine is registered as a queueable source that plays in time with the decks, not merely as a controller.

interconnect.name: MIDI 1.0
interconnect.verdict: Required baseline. Insufficient alone for high-resolution jog wheels.

interconnect.name: MIDI 2.0 / UMP
interconnect.resolution: Up to 32-bit values; 16 groups x 16 channels
interconnect.support: Windows 11 MIDI Services (2026), macOS CoreMIDI (since Oct 2021), Linux ALSA (kernel 6.5+, 2023)
interconnect.verdict: Adopt now. MIDI-CI Property Exchange (JSON-based) and Profiles allow controllers to describe themselves, which could largely automate mapping - a real leap past every current DJ app.

interconnect.name: HID
interconnect.resolution: Far beyond 128 steps/rotation; Serato mappings commonly use 1536 (128 x 12)
interconnect.support: Pioneer CDJs and most Serato/Traktor-certified hardware, via an 'Advanced' HID mode
interconnect.verdict: Needed for credible scratch feel. Mixxx already implements HID mapping with a packet-parser helper.

interconnect.name: MIDI Clock (24 PPQN)
interconnect.verdict: Primary outbound tempo path. Keep the clock path short and avoid Thru daisy-chains, which introduce jitter.

interconnect.name: MIDI Time Code (MTC)
interconnect.verdict: Positional reference only. Too coarse and too jitter-prone for beat-accurate musical triggering.

interconnect.name: Ableton Link
interconnect.role: Peer-to-peer tempo, beat, phase and start/stop sync over LAN
interconnect.resolution: Shared continuous timeline with a phase 'quantum'
interconnect.support: Traktor, djay, hundreds of iOS apps and hardware
interconnect.verdict: Adopt - the cable-free way for phones, laptops and hardware in the room to share our timeline. Licence caution: GPL-2.0-or-later unless commercially licensed from Ableton.

interconnect.name: OSC (Open Sound Control)
interconnect.verdict: Adopt via liblo (LGPL-2.1) for the bridge into lighting and visuals.

interconnect.name: DMX512 / Art-Net / sACN
interconnect.support: OLA, QLC+; rekordbox drives DMX via the RB-DMX1 interface
interconnect.verdict: Adopt through OLA. Phrase-aware auto-lighting, as in rekordbox Lighting mode, is the capability to match.

interconnect.name: Mackie Control / HUI
interconnect.support: Reverse-engineered spec; open implementations exist (TouchMCU, MusE)
interconnect.verdict: Optional. Unlocks a large installed base of motorised-fader surfaces that no DJ app currently addresses.

interconnect.name: Web MIDI API
interconnect.support: Chrome 43+, Edge 79+, Firefox 108+, Opera, Samsung Internet. NOT Safari on macOS/iOS, with no announced roadmap. Chrome 124+ gates the entire API behind a permission prompt and requires HTTPS.
interconnect.verdict: Convenience path only. Because Safari and therefore every iPhone browser is excluded, the native MIDI path must remain authoritative.
